## Your Edge

##### It is the simplest way to have an investing edge to outperforming the market.

Measuring the quality of earnings relative to investor expectations creates a superior measure of the Post-earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD) and, quite simply, those companies with favorable earnings and low expectations consistently outperform the market. ... and those with high expectations and weaker results **don't**.

From December 17, 2002 until April 17, 2026, the date of the last graded earnings release that has completed a quarter, we have graded 182,698 earnings releases. If you had randomly bought any of them at the open after their earnings release and held until the open following their next earnings release, you would have averaged 2.5% for the 13-week period. During the same period, there were 55,359 that we graded a D+ or lower and they averaged a gain of 0.3% for the quarter. **On the other hand, there were 64,327 with an Earnings Whisper Grade of B- or higher, and they averaged a 4.7% quarterly gain.**
